# A faulty GPU is not nvsnap's failure

Status: built (`internal/agent/gpu_probe.go`, the `probe` action of
`nvsnap-gpu-suspend`).

<!-- toc: generated by scripts/docs/docs-toc.py; edit the headings, not this list -->
**Contents**

- [Problem](#problem)

## Problem

A GPU that needs a reset (`NV_ERR_RESET_REQUIRED` in the kernel log) fails
every pod placed on it, with nvsnap or without. Before this change nvsnap
counted those failures against itself, for a whole configuration, on every
node:

1. **The library was blamed.** A pod that never started under the gpushare
   library marked its configuration `gpushare-failed`
   (`considerGPUShareFailure`, [CRIU-CAPTURE-FALLBACK](CRIU-CAPTURE-FALLBACK.md)).
   Every pod of that configuration then started without the library, and
   CRIU stopped capturing it, until a pod without the library failed the
   same way.
2. **A verified checkpoint was given up.** Restores that failed on bad GPUs
   (`restore=CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN`) counted toward
   `criuGroupMaxRestoreFailures`; at the limit the checkpoints were blocked
   and the configuration fell back to the cachedir, though the capture had
   restored and served before.

Neither counter asked whether the GPU under the failing pod works.

## Design

Before a failure counts, the agent of the failing pod's node probes the GPUs
the pod was given, without nvsnap.

**Which GPUs.** The pod's container runtime keeps the OCI spec the container
was created with, also after the container exited (a pod that crash-loops
has no running process to look at). The agent reads it through the CRI
(`Runtime.ContainerSpec`, containerd and CRI-O). The GPUs are the UUIDs in
`NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (the container toolkit's runtime hook), or else the
`/dev/nvidiaN` device nodes in the spec (CDI), mapped to UUIDs by the
driver's minor numbers (`/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information`). A spec
that names neither cannot tell.

**The probe.** `nvsnap-gpu-suspend --libcuda <host libcuda.so.1> probe`
runs in the agent's container, never in the workload, once per GPU with
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<UUID>`, all of a pod's GPUs at once, for at most 30
seconds each. It initialises the driver, opens the GPU's primary context,
fills a 1 MiB buffer, reads it back and checks it, and frees it. It prints
`ok`, or the step that failed and the driver's error name, and exits 0 or 2.
It exits 1 when it cannot ask the driver at all. One GPU per process keeps a
bad GPU from failing the probe of a good one: the driver's initialisation
covers every visible GPU.

**The verdict.** A GPU is *faulty* only when the probe ran and a step failed
with a hardware error: `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, `ECC_UNCORRECTABLE`,
`HARDWARE_STACK_ERROR`, `ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`, `ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`,
`LAUNCH_FAILED`, `NVLINK_UNCORRECTABLE`, `SYSTEM_NOT_READY`, a buffer that
read back wrong, or `NO_DEVICE` for a GPU the driver lists. Anything else is
*unknown*: the GPU busy or held (`DEVICES_UNAVAILABLE`, `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, as
under exclusive-process mode or a container still dying), a timeout, no
driver library, or the agent without `/dev/nvidiactl` or `/dev/nvidia-uvm`
(without them the driver answers `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` for any GPU, which
would be the agent's setup, not the GPU).

**What a faulty GPU changes.**

| Failure | Probe faulty | Healthy or unknown |
|---|---|---|
| A pod never starts under the library | No mark, and no mark cleared; the pod is left as it is | As before: mark (or clear) and replace |
| A lone restore that ran and failed | Not counted, checkpoint not blocked; the pod is replaced and restores again | As before |
| A group restore with a member on a faulty GPU | Not counted for the group, checkpoints not blocked; every placeholder is replaced and restores again | As before |
| A restored engine dies | Same as a failed restore | As before |

In each faulty case the agent logs the GPU, the step and the error, emits a
Warning event `NvsnapGPUFault` on the node, counts the probe in
`nvsnap_gpu_probes_total{result="faulty"}`, and (for restores) records the
fault on the group record (`gpuFaults`, `lastGPUFault`) and counts the
restore as `nvsnap_restore_outcomes_total{outcome="gpu-fault"}`. Nothing is
cordoned: the cluster's own health checks own that.

**Across agents.** A group restore's members are restored by their nodes'
agents (`POST /v1/restore`). The member's agent probes its placeholder's GPUs
after a failed restore and returns the faults in the `X-Nvsnap-Gpu-Fault`
header (JSON), which the driving agent reads back into the error; the
error's text is never parsed. An agent of an older release sends no header,
and its failures count as before.

## Why not

- **Counting failures on distinct GPUs.** That adds a failed pod cycle to
  every real fallback, and still blames nvsnap when the scheduler places both
  pods on bad GPUs, which a node with several bad GPUs makes likely.
- **Cordoning.** Not nvsnap's to decide; the event names the GPU for whoever
  is.
- **Bounding the restores that fail on faulty GPUs.** Falling back would not
  help: a pod on a faulty GPU fails without nvsnap too. Replacing a
  restore's pods gives the scheduler another placement, where a cold start
  on the same GPU would crash-loop where it is.

## Limits

- A healthy GPU can probe *unknown* (busy, held); its failure then counts, as
  before the probe. The probe never excuses a failure it cannot attribute.
- The probe needs the host's driver library reachable from the agent (a GPU
  Operator driver root under `/run/nvidia/driver`, or the host's library
  directories under the agent's `/host` mount). Without it every probe is
  *unknown*, the behaviour before the probe.
- The probe takes a GPU context for about a second. On a pod that is
  restarting at that moment, the workload's own start may see that memory
  in use.

## Tests

- `TestGPUProbeTool` builds the tool and runs its probe against a stand-in
  driver library failing at each step (`internal/agent/testdata/fake_libcuda.c`),
  through the agent's runner and verdict.
- `TestProbeVerdict`, `TestSpecGPUs`, `TestContainerIDOf`, `TestOnPodGPUFault`,
  `TestRestoreFailureCarriesGPUFaults`, `TestGroupRestoreFailureGPUFault`,
  `TestRecordGPUFault`.
- Each decision, faulty and healthy: `TestFailGroup_GPUFaultKeepsTheCapture`,
  `TestFailRestored_GPUFault`, `TestConsiderGPUShareFailure_FaultyGPU`.
- On a cluster: the probe on a healthy GPU and on one that needs a reset; the
  conformance gate with the bad GPUs in play (restores and library starts on
  them do not fall back, and the node events name them), and on a cluster
  without bad GPUs (the library-failure scenario must still fall back).
